findings.disposition_note: The defect costs no information and the panels are legible at the size the record serves them; the layout change is cosmetic and is left to a future figure pass rather than holding this node.
findings.summary: The panel that carries the whole subject occupies 239 of the figure's 1400 px width while the residual strip beneath it spans 1294 px, so about 83% of the canvas width is blank on either side of the contours. On the reckon page the same figure is served at roughly 900 px wide, which puts the poloidal panel at about 154 px: the 7 pt hollow EFIT null markers render at about 7 px and the individual contour lines at about 0.7 px, so the null-set geometry the panels exist to show is read only by zooming. Present identically in all three attached panels. Not blocking: nothing is clipped or hidden, and the artifact is a vector SVG that a reader can enlarge. The layout is the gridspec/figuresize choice at scripts/prototypes/diiid_vertical_loss/render_trip_panels.py:285-286, 289; placing the residual strip beside the panel rather than beneath it would give the contours about 1.5x the drawn height on the same canvas.

findings.disposition_note: Each panel is unambiguous alone and the set is read one figure at a time in the record; the formatting mismatch misleads no reading.
findings.summary: The same quantity is labelled to different precision across the three panels of one set: the frame-137 trip-2 strip is ticked '0.0' and '0.1' while both frame-146 strips are ticked '0.00' and '0.25'. The strip sets no tick formatter (strip.tick_params at scripts/prototypes/diiid_vertical_loss/render_trip_panels.py:460), so matplotlib's automatic locator decides the format per panel's data range. A reader comparing the three panels must notice that the tick precision and the axis step differ, and the 0.1114 mark in the first panel reads as 'just above 0.1' where the same kind of value in the others is quoted to two decimals. Not blocking: each panel's own axis is correct and the marks are unambiguous on their own page. A fixed format ('.2f') and a shared locator across the set would remove the inconsistency.

findings.disposition_note: The callout separation was introduced precisely to stop the two markers reading as one blob, and it does; the residual ambiguity of glyph identity costs no reading of position.
findings.summary: A solved X-point closer than 0.14 m to the axis is drawn at 0.7x its normal marker size (scripts/prototypes/diiid_vertical_loss/render_trip_panels.py:101), which at 110 dpi is about 5 pt or 7 px. In the attached frame-146 trip-1 panel the crowded saddle at (1.6697, -0.2755) renders as a small red dot immediately above the solved-axis triangle (measured clusters: callout 9x16 px including its leader, axis triangle 10x10 px, 4 px apart), so the mark cannot be matched by eye to the 'solved X-point' X in the legend. The leader line and the hollow dot at the true position are the only cues that it is an X-point. Not blocking: the pair is still separated rather than merged, and the leader points to the exact returned position, so no coordinate is lost.

findings.disposition_note: The caption carries the result in words and the absent contours are the measured state, not a drawing fault; the figure withholds no fact the record asserts.
findings.summary: In the frame-146 trip-2 panel the 'solved flux' series appears only above the limiter: every solved-flux pixel in that panel lies between y 101 and y 207, and the plasma body (core box x 680..800, y 210..430) contains 0 solved-flux px against 1983 EFIT px, where the two sibling panels carry 1409/948 and 1298/928 respectively. The comparison of the two fields, which is why both are drawn, is therefore unavailable in the core of this one panel, and the collapse the caption reports is communicated by the absence of blue contours. Not blocking: the absence is data (the solved field's shared contour levels admit no ring in the core) and the caption states the result in words, so no claim rests on a reader inferring it from the picture alone. A reader who does not know that could read the all-grey body as a rendering omission.

item_verdicts.caption_independence: No caption only repeats a title. None of the three figures carries a title (identity is in the file name and the caption), and each caption states the frame, trip, axis position, fraction of Ip confined and the mask-change count, so each adds information the picture does not carry.
item_verdicts.finding_materiality: Four findings, all non-blocking; none of the blocking categories is met. No label is clipped (measured outer margin at least 14 px on every edge of every render), no label overlaps another label or the data, no text is unreadable (lowest text contrast about 7.8:1), and no figure depicts information that is naturally a table.
item_verdicts.rendered_artifact: All three attached PNGs were opened and read as images, and the measurements quoted in this record were taken from those same files. No SVG was opened and no other image was opened or rendered. The attachment-to-figure map is derived from the attachments' own content and cross-checked against the committed per-trip-panels.json residuals.
item_verdicts.scope: Read-only. No file was edited, created, moved, deleted, redrawn, relabelled or reformatted. The only writes are this record at its two declared paths and the run manifest. One scratch decoder for reading PNG pixels was written under the run's TMPDIR scratch directory and reads only the three named attachments.
